clue.text: Bits of music naturally fitting into second verse occasionally

indicators.note: something fitting into a space sits inside it, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
natch is informal shorthand for naturally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so just every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of verse

explanation.surface: A song's snippets of melody slot neatly into its second verse now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Natch is informal British and American slang, a clipped form of naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatches are short fragments, as in hearing snatches of a tune or conversation.

clue.text: New word maybe describing an object briefly covering part of the eye

indicators.note: briefly asks for a word cut short, losing its final letter
covering means wrapping around, so the shortened word goes either side of the other piece

parts.note: a noun names an object; shortened by its last letter
the uvea is the pigmented middle layer of the eye

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson pairing a new term with an anatomy note about the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The truncated word splits after its second letter so the eye part fits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouveau is the French adjective borrowed into English for recent or newly arrived, as in nouveau riche.

clue.text: Sin that isn't corrected immediately

indicators.note: something corrected has been put right by rearranging it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A moral demand: any sin that isn't put right must be dealt with at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning right now, without any delay.

clue.text: Loads of clapped-out motors

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a scrapyard full of old cars; 'clapped-out' is British slang for worn out, and 'motors' are cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps means lots in informal speech, and a heap is also slang for a battered old car.

clue.text: Reproduction of letters in lines cut at the edges?

definitions.text: Reproduction of letters in lines cut at the edges?

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade copy, so the letters are put together afresh in a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word lines, taken as written

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, the only ones kept here

parts.note: the first and last letters of cut

explanation.surface: Copying out lettering whose lines have been trimmed at their borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the thing: a stencil reproduces letters through shapes cut out of a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet used to reproduce lettering by painting through its openings.

clue.text: Chief allowed to carry key for holiday home

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the pair

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for chief
A is a musical key
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A boss is permitted to bring a key along to the holiday cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces together do the carrying, with the key held between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin of the Swiss kind, often rented for holidays.

clue.text: Short opportunity to acquire horse and vehicle it could pull

indicators.note: short asks for the word to be trimmed of its final letter
acquiring something means taking it in, so the horse goes inside

parts.note: chance, cut short
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A brief chance to buy a horse and the carriage it could draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to the horse: a charabanc was once horse-drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an open long-bodied coach, originally horse-drawn, used for outings.

clue.text: Somewhat exhilarating, up-and-coming boxer

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top
somewhat means only a part, so the letters lie inside a longer word

parts.note: the letters inside exhILArating

explanation.surface: A promising young boxer described as rather thrilling to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming' looks like praise for a newcomer, but in this down clue it sends the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight champion fighter.

clue.text: No good ignoring brutal execution in each country

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: stoning is a brutal method of execution
NG is shorthand for no good

explanation.surface: A grim comment on capital punishment, ignoring any good in it, in every nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' is not dismissive comment but two letters to remove from the execution method.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, the northernmost of the three Baltic republics.

clue.text: Group of colleges subsequently very famous for promoting individual policies

parts.note: a university is a group of colleges
later means subsequently
A-list describes the most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: A university later becomes renowned for championing go-it-alone policies.
explanation.definitionFit: A unilateralist favours one-sided action, such as a nation disarming without waiting for others.

clue.text: Class containing one hugely intelligent person

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a genus is a biological class or kind
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A school class that includes one exceptionally bright pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is someone of exceptional intellectual or creative power.

clue.text: Freewheeling firm introducing a scam

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
taken as written
a sting is a confidence trick

explanation.surface: A careless business launching a fraud without a second thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasting means moving without power, as a cyclist freewheels downhill.

clue.text: Going around Euston a bit after initially touring Camden Town?

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word only

parts.note: the first letter of touring

explanation.surface: Wandering around Euston for a while after first sightseeing in Camden Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston and Camden Town are both stops on the London Underground, known as the Tube; the question mark marks Camden Town as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Camden Town is one example of a stop on London's Underground railway network.

clue.text: Endless search to get a pickle to accompany ace Mexican dish

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: quest, losing its last letter
taken as written
dill is a pickled cucumber, short for dill pickle
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A never-ending hunt for a pickle to serve alongside a great Mexican meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A quesadilla is a tortilla folded around melted cheese, a Mexican snack.

clue.text: Outside the city, find it's unusually clean

indicators.note: outside places the other letters around this short piece
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words
EC, the postcode, stands for the City of London

explanation.surface: Out of town, someone finds things are remarkably clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FIND IT'S go round EC and the whole is mixed; 'the city' means the City of London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect is to clean thoroughly, killing germs.

clue.text: Go to bash?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a heart goes, it pulses steadily

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an invitation to a party, a bash; really it pairs two verbs, one for pulsing and one for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both throbbing rhythmically, as a heart goes, and hitting something repeatedly.

clue.text: Small island between two areas where most people live

indicators.note: between places the pair of letters with one piece on each side

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, taken twice
S for small and I for island

explanation.surface: A tiny island lying between two heavily populated regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia holds roughly six in ten of the world's population, more than every other continent combined.

clue.text: Patient measurement system mostly covers the majority of work

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter goes
the majority means more than half but not all, so the final letter is dropped
covering something means wrapping around it

parts.note: a scale is a system of measurement; cut short
toil is hard work; cut short

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's measuring system mostly covers most of the work involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like a noun for someone in hospital but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stoical means enduring hardship without complaint, a synonym for patient.

clue.text: Keep being swept away by the tide, perhaps?

definitions.text: Keep being swept away by the tide, perhaps?

parts.words: Keep being swept away by the tide, perhaps?
parts.note: surface reading: a fortress or its stronghold tower lost to the sea
setter's reading: a keep is a castle's tower, and this one is made of something the tide easily washes off a beach

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb (keep being swept away) but is the noun for a castle stronghold, one built on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's beach model of a fortress is washed away when the sea comes in.

clue.text: Pronouncement of growth dismissed, for sure

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the answer matches the sound of the words

parts.note: a node is a growth or lump, and dismissed batsmen are out

explanation.surface: A medical declaration that a lump has been cleared, said with certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning certainly, without question.

clue.text: Accountant dipping into money from nearby residents

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant helping himself to cash collected from the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sourced locally comes from the surrounding area and the people living close by.

clue.text: In the end, commenters online had to accept frequently getting moderated

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a piece goes inside
in the end points to the final letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the last letters of commenters, online and had
often means frequently

explanation.surface: Eventually, people posting online had to accept that they were often being moderated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'moderated' suggests forum moderators; here it means toned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be moderated is to be made less extreme, toned down, which is what softened means.

clue.text: Bishop provided guidance for church office

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ran as in managed or directed
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bishop gave direction on the running of a church office.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local office of a larger organisation, as a bank branch.

clue.text: Language graduate given books by university

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
U for university, placed by the rest

explanation.surface: A language graduate presented with textbooks by their university.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of related languages spoken across southern and central Africa.

clue.text: Momentous, violent alien conquest

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A science-fiction headline: an alien invasion of earth would be historic.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequential describes something important, with significant effects or results.

clue.text: Problem failing at first to cause discomfort

indicators.note: failing at the start means losing the opening letter

parts.note: a snag is a problem or hitch

explanation.surface: A problem that initially fails to cause any discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to bother persistently, as a nagging pain or worry troubles someone.

clue.text: Insignificant landmark bordering loch

indicators.note: bordering means lying around the edges, so this piece wraps the other

parts.note: a sight is a landmark worth seeing
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A minor tourist attraction on the shore of a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means small or trivial in degree, of little importance.

clue.text: Returning desire to be involved in series of matches and competitions

parts.note: a tour is a series of matches played abroad by a touring team

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A renewed wish to take part in sports fixtures and contests.
